howto.goal: The goal of the game is to connect two words by adding and removing words within them using as few guesses and hints as possible.
howto.graphAnyWord: You can guess from any word you have already found, not just the last one. The game ends when you complete the path between the words, but you can double-back, work from both ends, leave dead ends, etc.
howto.graphSpine: The golden center line, or <add>"spine"</add> of the graph is the shortest path between the two words you're trying to bridge. The rest of the graph are a subset of the words surrounding the spine that provide a few possible alternative paths. All <wordlists>valid words</wordlists> can be guessed, so the nodes you see when the game start are not the only paths between the words! If you guess a word that's not on the graph yet, it will be added and connected to any other words that it can reach.
howto.hintsBody: Tap or click an undiscovered node to receive a <w>hint</w> for it. You can't get length or letter hints for words on the spine or on shortcuts - only hints about whether the word can be reached by adding or removing a word. Hints are unlimited, and counted alongside your guesses. First you will see the number of letters in the word, and then each subsequent tap will reveal another letter. This is not a competitive game, go ahead and do a thousand hints, challenge yourself and use no hints, whatever.
howto.ruleActive: The player selects a revealed word in the graph to be the "active word"
howto.ruleAddRemove: Each turn you either <add>add</add> or <cut>remove</cut> a word from the active word.
howto.ruleContiguous: The letters you add or remove must be contiguous
howto.ruleMinSub: Words added or removed to reach new words must be {min, plural, one {# letter} other {# letters}} or longer
howto.ruleMinWord: Words within the graph must be {min, plural, one {# letter} other {# letters}} or longer
howto.rulePosition: The added or removed word can be in any position - before, after, and especially inside the other words.
howto.ruleRemainder: The letters that are left after adding or removing must also be a word, and that becomes the next active word.
howto.ruleValidWord: The letters you add or remove must be a single valid word.
howto.shortcutsFound: If your guess stumbles you onto a shortcut, the shortcut path will appear and be highlighted and be all shiny to let you know that the rest of the shortcut is possible.
howto.shortcutsWhat: The ability to guess rare words means that some boards have <add>shortcuts</add> - paths between the two target words that are shorter than the par score, which is computed from the smaller word list.
howto.shortcutsWhy: The puzzle tries to be "playable" by using a smaller list of more common words, since it's not fun to get sniped by a squirrelly rare word. However, also to make the game "playable," we want to allow all words that someone might consider real because it's frustrating to guess a real word and have it be refused.

tutorial.boardAround: Around it are words that lead somewhere without being shortest. Every puzzle has many non-spine paths between the target words - a winning path does not need to touch the spine!
tutorial.boardSpine: The gold line down the middle is the "spine" - the shortest way through using only common words. Its words are unnamed dots for now.
tutorial.bothEndsAny: You can guess from any word you have reached - including the goal - by tapping it.
tutorial.bothEndsAsk: Tap towing to guess from it.
tutorial.bothEndsWhy: Working from both ends is often easier: <w>towing</w> is <w>to·wing</w>, and taking <cut>to</cut> off gets us to "wing" which seems like the right direction.
tutorial.finishBody: Finish the game by reaching towing through the shortcut!
tutorial.finishJoin: Now finish the game by completing the connection to towing!
tutorial.firstMoveWhere: The word with a gold ring around it is the word you are guessing from. Make moves by typing in the guess box.
tutorial.firstMoveWhich: The next spine word after <w>showing</w> is <w>shadowing</w>, made by putting <add>ad</add> in the middle of it like <w>sh·</w><add>ad</add><w>·owing</w>
tutorial.firstMoveWhole: Type the whole word you are guessing, not the piece. The game works out which piece you meant.
tutorial.hintRouteAsk: Click the gold dot to show a - hint.
tutorial.hintRouteAskMore: Once more for the hell of it.
tutorial.hintRouteAskPlus: Click the gold dot until you get a + hint.
tutorial.hintRouteRead: So a <cut>−</cut> here means to reach this word from <w>shadowing</w>, we have to remove a word, and vice versa for the <add>+</add>.
tutorial.hintRouteWhat: Spine hints tell you how to reach a word from another. <add>+</add> by adding letters, <cut>−</cut> by taking them away.
tutorial.hintRouteWhy: A spine word doesn't hint its length or letters, that would be too easy!
tutorial.hintWordAgain: Click it again to reveal a letter.
tutorial.hintWordAsk: Click the lit dot to reveal its length.
tutorial.hintWordBody: You can get hints for any undiscovered node! For non-spine nodes, the first click gives its length; every click after that reveals one more random letter.
tutorial.hintWordMore: Keep revealing letters or move on
tutorial.lineTicks: The tickmarks perpendicular from the edge of a node are an indicator of the "degree" of the node, or how many other nodes connect to it - the number of ticks isn't literal (i.e. there are more than 4 other words that can be reached from <w>showing</w>), but more ticks means higher degree.
tutorial.lineWritten: The move is written along the edge: <add>+ad</add>, in gold (or <cut>red</cut> if a word was removed).
tutorial.name: Tutorial
tutorial.offBoardAsk: Name a word that's not on the board yet.
tutorial.offBoardFamily: You are standing on <w>wing</w>. Two letters on the front of it is a whole family: <add>se</add>, <add>mo</add>, <add>vo</add>, <add>ca</add>.
tutorial.offBoardWhat: The starting nodes on the board are a suggestion, but any word you can reach is valid. Guessing a word that isn't on the board adds it, along with any of its neighbors that might form a new route.
tutorial.parRelax: Lower numbers of guesses and hints are better, but this isn't a competitive game: both are unlimited, and there's no penalty to wander off and explore the board. Especially if you're new, don't worry about keeping a tidy board or making optimal guesses. Take some time to fill in the board with guesses to get a feel for the game. If you're frustrated, get more hints!
tutorial.parWhat: <w>par</w> is the shortest way through using ordinary words: four moves here. Your guesses and hints are counted beside it.
tutorial.shortcutAsk: Tap showing to stand on it.
tutorial.shortcutThis: This one does: <w>showing</w> is <cut>sh</cut><w>·owing</w>: Rare words aren't always long, "<w>sh</w>" is a word but not a very common one. take <cut>sh</cut> off the front, and the rest of the way through is drawn for you in gold.
tutorial.shortcutWhy: Par is measured over ordinary words, but you probably know lots of words that aren't so common! Sometimes there are shortcut paths through rare words, the header says when a board has one.
tutorial.statementGoal: The goal of the game is to connect the two target words by guessing some path between them using as few guesses and hints as possible.
tutorial.statementWhat: The puzzle is stated at the top: connect <w>showing</w> and <w>towing</w>. You can move from any revealed node, so you can work from either end, backtrack and make a new branch, whatever.
tutorial.welcomeRule: Every move takes one whole word out of another, or puts one in. What is left has to be a word too.
tutorial.welcomeShape: The piece you add or take out must be a word, must be in one run, and can sit anywhere - including in the middle.
tutorial.wrongBoardBody: It is taught on one particular puzzle, <w>{id}</w>, and a rebuild that changed that puzzle’s answer changed its address. Point <w>LESSON.puzzle</w> at a board that is still there, and rewrite the steps that name its words.
tutorial.wrongBoardTitle: The tutorial’s board is not in this bank
welcome.offer: There is a short walkthrough on a real board. It takes a couple of minutes.
welcome.title: New here?
welcome.what: The game is getting from one word to another by adding or removing a whole word from inside it.
welcome.whereItWent: It stays in the menu, under “Tutorial”.
